entries.subject: Celestia native nucleus illustration and catalog scale
entries.finding: Superseded 2026-09-16: the Celestia generic mesh was a shared illustration with no relation to this nucleus, and its catalogue radius was an estimate. The package now shows a smooth ellipsoid at the published effective radius (Campins and Fernández (2002), Earth, Moon and Planets 89, 117); no mesh from Celestia is retained.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured shape model of this nucleus (radar, spacecraft or a convex lightcurve inversion with a stated pole) would replace the ellipsoid.

entries.subject: Published event and observation context
entries.finding: Retained intake decision: IRAS–Araki–Alcock was discovered in 1983 by the IRAS satellite and two independent observers. Its name records all three discoveries. The cited material supplies explanatory context; it does not qualify photographic terrain on this nucleus.

entries.subject: Published effective nucleus radius
entries.finding: Campins and Fernández (2002), Earth, Moon and Planets 89, 117: effective radius 4.6 km ± 0.5. Radar shows a strongly non-spherical nucleus a few kilometres across (Harmon et al. 1989); no axis ratio is adopted here. Used as the volume-equivalent radius of the displayed ellipsoid.
